Hi all 

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, details below.

- Logging/payloads: For Redwood Private deployed inside a customer-managed VPC we do not send request payloads or logs to Redwood-managed storage by default. All telemetry can be configured to stay within your account and forwarded only to your S3/Athena or equivalent. The default behavior for hosted Redwood is different, but not relevant for Private deployments.

- Deployment models: We support two private models: 1) Redwood Private (control plane managed by Redwood, data plane in customer VPC via customer-managed subnets & IAM roles), and 2) On-prem / air-gapped package (full control plane + data plane deployed on-prem) for highly regulated customers. Both options can be configured to block outbound internet access.

- Egress controls: You can restrict outbound via VPC routing policies, NAT (or no NAT), VPC endpoints for private S3 access, and controlled DNS via Route 53 Resolver rules. We also support explicit allowlists for external services (e.g., model artifact repos) and can ship model artifacts to your object storage to avoid external pulls. OS/patching in air-gapped mode is handled via customer-provided update bundles or an approved offline media process.

Detailed notes (for your security team):
1) Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ for all inter-service traffic. Option to require mTLS between service components.
2) Data at rest: Customer-managed KMS keys supported for model caches and any persisted telemetry. By default, model weights are read-only on local attached storage and can be staged from customer S3.
3) Logging & retention: Runtime logs (metrics, slow-path telemetry) can be sent to a customer-owned S3 bucket/CloudWatch with configurable retention. Request payloads (user inputs) are not persisted in Redwood-managed systems for customer-managed VPCs unless explicitly enabled for debugging; we can provide sanitized debug exports under controlled process.
4) Egress prevention: We recommend deployment with no NAT gateway and explicit VPC endpoints for required services. We provide a small egress watchdog that can alert on attempted outbound connections; for air-gapped setups that component is disabled and audits are done via offline logs.

Action items I can take before the call:
- Produce a redlined VPC diagram showing recommended subnet layout, endpoints, and routing (I updated the attached PDF with notes).
- Provide a short checklist for procurement/procurement security: KMS configuration, IAM policies, SAML/SCIM integration notes, and a minimal SOW template.

If that works I can join a 45-minute tech review with your infra/security folks  propose Mon/Tue next week.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks

Hi Jamie / team 

Adding a few security/compliance-specific clarifications to Dylan's excellent summary:

- PHI/PII handling: We treat request payloads as potentially sensitive. For customer-managed VPCs, we provide configuration flags that ensure no request payloads are sent to Redwood-managed telemetry. Any debug collection requires an explicit, auditable opt-in with time-limited retention and approval by your security contact.
- Audit logs: We can stream audit logs (admin actions, model deploy events, key rotation events) to your CloudWatch/Splunk/S3 with integrity controls (signing) and recommended 365-day retention by default; retention periods can be tuned per account.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS is required for production PII workloads; HSM integration can be supported for enterprise customers (we have partners for AWS CloudHSM and third-party HSMs).
- SOC2 / evidence: We can provide SOC2 Type II reports and a security questionnaire. For statements about data never leaving the customer VPC, we'll provide a deployment attestation and run a short validation during the POC to demonstrate no external egress.

Please let us know the minimum acceptable retention windows for logs and any specific controls (e.g., IP restrictions, source address tagging) you require and we'll incorporate them in the MAP.

-Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
